newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota spring wheat harvest speeds ahead.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota spring wheat harvest speeds ahead.

text.p: Clear skies and warm days in Minnesota allowed good advances in the wheat and barley harvests in the week ended August 25, the Minnesota Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly update.

Due to a reporting error last week, it revised spring wheat harvest progress. As of Sunday, spring wheat was 47 percent harvested against a revised 35 percent a week earlier. The service originally said 63 percent of the harvest was complete the week before last. Average a year ago last week was 51 percent harvested and last year spring wheat was 63 percent harvested.
The spring wheat crop was rated 53 percent good to excellent, down two points, and 38 percet fair.
Barley was 53 percent harvested as of Sunday against 36 last week, 58 last year and 65 average. The crop was rated 61 percent good to excellent, 22 fair and 16 percent poor.
Corn ratings held steady at 57 percent good to excellent and 33 percent fair. The crop adavanced to 33 percent in the dough stage against 15 last week but lagged 57 percent last year and 55 average.

Soybean condition ratings improved to 59 percent good to excellent, up three points on the week. Ninety-five percent of the crop was setting pods and 8 percent was turning color, both several points ahead of the five-year average.
The agency said rain in the southern part of the state provided some relief to moisture-stressed row crops. "More moisture is still needed to finish the crop," it said.
Topsoil moisture rated adequate to surplus fell four points to 58 percent.
Oats harvested were 93 percent versus 78 week ago and 80 average.
Sunflower conditions were rated 50 percent good to excellent and 33 percent fair.
